PhenoRec Tutorial: Phenotype-Preserving Integration of scATAC-seq Data

In this tutorial, we demonstrate how to use PhenoRec for phenotype-preserving integration of single-cell chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) data.

Here, we use a type 2 diabetes (T2D) snATAC-seq dataset from GEO accession GSE169453. The dataset was generated from human pancreatic islet samples profiled using the 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell ATAC platform and includes nondiabetic and T2D donors. For this tutorial, we randomly subsampled 100,000 cells for illustration purposes.

The tutorial consists of four main stages:

  1. Preprocess the scATAC-seq data.
  2. Estimate latent cell states.
  3. Apply PhenoRec to recover phenotype-associated signals.
  4. Visualize the phenotype-preserving integrated data.

1 Load required packages

We first load PhenoRec together with the packages required for this tutorial.

library(PhenoRec)
library(Matrix)
library(data.table)
library(Signac)
library(Seurat)

2 Load data

We load the chromatin accessibility matrix and cell-level metadata.

atac_count <- readRDS("T2D_data.RDS")
metadata <- readRDS("T2D_metadata.RDS")

The accessibility matrix contains genomic regions as rows and cells as columns. The metadata contain sample/batch identity (donor), phenotype information (Diabetes.status), and cell-type annotations (cell_type).

We construct a Signac chromatin assay from the accessibility matrix and then create a Seurat object.

seurat_data <- CreateChromatinAssay(
  counts = atac_count,
  sep = c("-", "-")
)

seurat_data <- CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = seurat_data,
  assay = "ATAC",
  meta.data = metadata
)

3 Preprocess the scATAC-seq data

For scATAC-seq data, we use the TF-IDF and latent semantic indexing (LSI) workflow implemented in Signac. If you are unfamiliar with this workflow, please refer to the official tutorial.

seurat_data <- RunTFIDF(seurat_data)
## Performing TF-IDF normalization
seurat_data <- RunSVD(
  seurat_data,
  n = 150,
  features = rownames(seurat_data)
)
## Running SVD
## Scaling cell embeddings

The first LSI component in scATAC-seq data is often strongly associated with sequencing depth. We therefore examine the correlation between LSI dimensions and ATAC sequencing depth.

DepthCor(
  seurat_data,
  assay = "ATAC",
  reduction = "lsi",
  n = 60
)

In this example, the first LSI dimension shows a strong association with sequencing depth.

We construct a UMAP representation using LSI dimensions 2–50.

seurat_data <- RunUMAP(
  object = seurat_data,
  reduction = "lsi",
  dims = 2:50
)
## Warning: The default method for RunUMAP has changed from calling Python UMAP via reticulate to the R-native UWOT using the cosine metric

The UMAP embedding can be colored by cell type, sample, and phenotype.

DimPlot(
  seurat_data,
  group.by = "cell_type",
  label = TRUE
) +
  DimPlot(
    seurat_data,
    group.by = "donor"
  ) +
  DimPlot(
    seurat_data,
    group.by = "Diabetes.status"
  )

The donor-colored UMAP reveals substantial sample-specific batch variation in the unintegrated data, with cells from the same sample tending to cluster together and cell-type structure poorly resolved. The phenotype-colored UMAP shows how cells are distributed across the phenotype groups

4 Estimate latent cell states

PhenoRec first requires an estimate of the underlying cell-state representation, denoted by (Z) in the PhenoRec model. In the current workflow, conventional integration with Harmony is used to obtain this representation.

Harmony is applied to LSI dimensions 2–150 using donor as the batch variable. The first LSI dimension is excluded because of its strong association with sequencing depth.

harmony_z <- harmony::RunHarmony(
  seurat_data@reductions$lsi@cell.embeddings[, 2:150],
  seurat_data@meta.data,
  "donor"
)
## Transposing data matrix
## Initializing state using k-means centroids initialization
## Warning: did not converge in 25 iterations
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Warning: Quick-TRANSfer stage steps exceeded maximum (= 5000000)
## Harmony 1/10
## Harmony 2/10
## Harmony converged after 2 iterations

We store this representation in the Seurat object under the reduction name estimate_z.

seurat_data[["estimate_z"]] <- CreateDimReducObject(
  embeddings = harmony_z,
  key = "estimatez_"
)
## Warning: No assay specified, setting assay as RNA by default.
## Warning: Adding a dimensional reduction (estimate_z) without the associated
## assay being present

The reduction name estimate_z is required by the current implementation of PhenoRec, which retrieves the estimated latent cell states from this reduction.

5 Encode batch and phenotype information

PhenoRec requires encoded matrices of categorical batch and phenotype variables. These are generated using encoding_function().

encoding_data <- encoding_function(
  seurat_data = seurat_data,
  batch_id = "donor",
  phenotype_id = "Diabetes.status"
)

Here, donor specifies the sample/batch variable, whereas Diabetes.status specifies the biological phenotype of interest.

6 Run PhenoRec

We now apply PhenoRec to the scATAC-seq data.

input_data <- list(
  atac_data = seurat_data,
  encoding_data = encoding_data
)
PhenoRec_result <- PhenoRec_ATAC(
  input = input_data,
  ncores = 30
)

ncores specifies the number of parallel worker used during feature-wise Bernoulli model fitting. Choose this value according to the computational resources available on your system.

The principal output for downstream analysis is:

integrated_data <- PhenoRec_result$integrated_data

integrated_data contains the PhenoRec-recovered chromatin accessibility data, with cells represented by rows and genomic regions by columns. This integrated data removes unwanted batch variation while preserving biologically meaningful phenotype-associated variation.

7 Visualize the PhenoRec-recovered data

We create a new Seurat object containing the PhenoRec-recovered chromatin accessibility data.

integrated_assay <- CreateAssayObject(
  data = t(integrated_data)
)

integrated_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = integrated_assay,
  assay = "ATAC",
  meta.data = seurat_data@meta.data
)
## Warning: Layer counts isn't present in the assay object; returning NULL

We scale the recovered accessibility values and compute PCA and UMAP.

integrated_obj <- ScaleData(integrated_obj)
## Centering and scaling data matrix
## Warning: Layer counts isn't present in the assay object; returning NULL
integrated_obj <- RunPCA(
  integrated_obj,
  features = rownames(integrated_obj)
)

We visualize the UMAP by cell type, sample, and phenotype.

DimPlot(
  integrated_obj,
  group.by = "cell_type",
  label = TRUE
) +
  DimPlot(
    integrated_obj,
    group.by = "donor"
  ) +
  DimPlot(
    integrated_obj,
    group.by = "Diabetes.status"
  )

This integrated representation preserves biologically meaningful phenotype signals and can be used to identify cell populations exhibiting pronounced state changes across phenotypes.
